title: Genie ASR benchmark manifest entry
description: One utterance in the genie_asr_benchmark corpus. `audio_file` is null for every entry as of this schema's authoring — see README.md's BLOCKED ON AUDIO SAMPLES note. `transcript_text` lets the resolver half of the pipeline (resolver.js) be exercised and scored today, independent of audio.

language.description: BCP-47-ish tag of the spoken language this utterance represents, e.g. 'en-IN', 'kn-IN', 'sa-IN', 'hi-IN', 'mixed'.

transcript_text.description: The utterance as clean written text (what a human would say). This is NOT a claimed ASR transcript — it is the resolver's input for a text-only accuracy pass. A separate `asr_noise_variant` may simulate a messy ASR transcript of the same utterance.

asr_noise_variant.description: Optional deliberately-messy variant of transcript_text (e.g. a known confusion pattern like 'Sumadha' for 'Sumadhva') used to test the resolver's ASR-confusion normalization specifically.

audio_file.description: Relative path under audio/<category>/ to a real recorded utterance. Null until real recordings are provided — see README.md.

notes.description: Free-text context, e.g. which real corpus entry this targets and why.

target_pattern.description: Regex the resolved `target` must match (realSlug for a grantha, or a parampara node's display name for a person). Null when no specific target is expected (e.g. a deterministic settings/renderer/audio action).

parameters.description: Expected subset of resolved `parameters` (e.g. {"reference": "1.1"}). Only listed keys are checked.

min_confidence.description: Resolved confidence must be >= this for the match to count as a pass (default 0 = any).

max_confidence.description: Optional upper bound — used for the ambiguous-commands category, where staying BELOW threshold and surfacing candidates is the correct behavior, not a wrong single guess.
